title: After Effects Expression Reference (full offline edition)
author: Docs for Adobe (community-maintained expression reference)
why: The whole expression API on one page: every global, time-conversion, vector, interpolation and random method, Comp/Layer/Property/Key/MarkerKey objects, sourceRectAtTime, loopOut types, TextStyle setters (setFontSize, setFillColor...), path methods, plus worked examples and changelog to AE 26.0; the agent can look up any function and its exact signature.

title: Syntax differences between expression engines
author: Adobe Help Center
why: JavaScript-engine pitfalls with fixes: if/else must end in else, no same-line if/else without braces, no trailing function declaration, thisLayer() not this(), .value needed for Source Text character indexing, posterizeTime(0) to freeze a value; explains most 'expression error' failures an agent will hit.

title: Realistic Bounce and Overshoot
author: Dan Ebberts (MotionScript.com)
why: The canonical inertial-overshoot and bounce expressions (amp/freq/decay off velocityAtTime at the last key, plus physically based bounce with elasticity) with line-by-line reasoning; gives UI cards and type a premium settle without hand-keying.

title: Triggering Animation with Markers (Expressioneer's Design Guide)
author: Dan Ebberts (MotionScript.com)
why: Time-remap expression that plays named, pre-keyed actions inside a precomp whenever a layer marker with that comment appears; the standard way to drive repeatable beats (host gestures, callouts) from VO markers.

title: Physical Simulations: Sine and Cosine
author: Dan Ebberts (MotionScript.com)
why: Math.sin/Math.cos as expression oscillators: amplitude, frequency in cycles per second (2*PI*freq*time), 90-degree phase offset, oscillation added on top of keyframed Position, with graphed examples and code; the base for pulses, sways and orbits.

title: Everything About Expressions You Didn't Know...Part 1: Beginning()
author: Zack Lovatt (School of Motion)
why: Property/Effect, Layer, Key and MarkerKey menus with code: wiggling and smoothing any property, reading precomp sources and in/out points, sampleImage colour picking, and a marker-duration time-remap that retimes a precomp to each marker.

title: Everything About Expressions You Didn't Know...Part Deux: Semicolon's Revenge
author: Zack Lovatt (School of Motion)
why: Light, Camera and Text menus with code: keep layer size constant during camera zooms, auto-focus DOF on a layer, set fonts and copy text styling by expression.

title: Everything About Expressions You Didn't Know...Part III: The Return of Math
author: Zack Lovatt (School of Motion)
why: JavaScript Math, Random Numbers and Path Property menus with code: rounding, min/max, sine waves, seedRandom per layer, copying and building shape paths (points, createPath).

title: Everything About Expressions You Didn't Know...Part Quatro: Going Global
author: Zack Lovatt (School of Motion)
why: Global, Comp, Footage and Project menus with code: linking across comps and layers, animating without keyframes, posterizeTime for stepped frame rates, timeToFrames/framesToTime, fit-to-comp scaling.

title: Everything About Expressions You Didn't Know...Part Chamesh: Interpolate This
author: Zack Lovatt (School of Motion)
why: Interpolation, Vector Math and Color Conversion menus with code: linear()/ease() as keyframe replacements and value remappers, clamp-limited wiggle, lookAt rotation, distance-driven animation, HSL/hex colour maths.

title: Anchor Point Expressions in After Effects
author: Ryan Plummer (School of Motion)
why: sourceRectAtTime top/left/width/height arithmetic for pinning the anchor to any corner or centre of a text layer, with a slider offset; the layout maths under responsive titles and boxes.

title: sourceRectAtTime(); | After Effects Expressions
author: Jake In Motion
why: Definitive 35-minute deep dive on sourceRectAtTime: what it returns, building boxes and accents that resize and follow animated text, and handling scale. Pre-2021, but the API is unchanged and nothing newer is as complete.

title: Intro to Expression Rigs in After Effects
author: School of Motion
why: Nol Honig and Zack Lovatt (Advanced Motion Methods) build rigs from a controller null with angle, checkbox and slider controls linked by expressions, then a larger multi-layer rig; under 50k views, but top-tier instructors and 4.4% likes.

title: ValueAtTime Expression- Adobe After Effects tutorial
author: ECAbrams
why: valueAtTime explained: referencing a leader layer at an offset time, building animated trails with a custom delay, and alternative trail methods; manual captions, so it reads cleanly.

title: Keyframe interpolation
author: Adobe Help Center
why: The missing interpolation reference: temporal vs spatial, Linear/Bezier/Continuous/Auto Bezier/Hold, the Keyframe Interpolation dialog, the Default Spatial Interpolation To Linear preference, boomerang-path fix, roving keys.

title: You NEED to understand spatial interpolation \\ After Effects Tutorial
author: Jake In Motion
why: Why layers drift between hold poses (Auto Bezier spatial interpolation), the fix with linear spatial keys, and the 3D case; under 50k views, but a top instructor at 5.3% likes, and it fills a gap nothing in the library covers.

title: Unlock the power of Keyframes in After Effects \\ AE Tutorial
author: Jake In Motion
why: Each keyframe type in practice (linear, bezier, auto/continuous bezier, eased, hold, rove across time) and lesser-known uses such as hold-key stepping and smear frames.

title: Layer markers and composition markers
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Marker mechanics for VO sync: add during audio preview with numpad *, durations, comments, colour labels, Update Markers From Source on precomps, how nested comp markers become layer markers.

title: Assorted animation tools
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Reference for Convert Audio to Keyframes (Audio Amplitude layer and channels), Smoother, Wiggler, Motion Sketch, path-to-motion and comp motion-blur settings (shutter angle/phase, samples).

title: Time-stretching and time-remapping
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Time remap, freeze frames, reverse, stretch-without-keyframes and frame blending modes; the mechanics behind marker-driven precomp retiming.

title: After Effects: Trigger Animations with Markers (No Keyframes)
author: Creative Dojo
why: Replaces in/out keyframes with expressions that read layer markers (accessing markers, fade and position animations timed from them), so moving a marker retimes the animation; the base pattern for VO-cued graphics. Niche topic, 2.4% likes.

title: How to Sync Animation With Audio Using Expressions in After Effects
author: ukramedia (Andrew Marston)
why: Convert Audio to Keyframes, then a rig that normalises by the track's max value, remaps with linear() and smooths the result; music-synced motion for idents and beat hits. Niche advanced, 2.8% likes.

title: Color management
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Working space, linearize/1.0-gamma blending, Interpret Footage colour (Preserve RGB, 16-235 profiles), output profiles, Convert to Linear Light, colour-managed video formats, and the washed-out/levels troubleshooting notes.

title: Quicktime Gamma Shift Bug - What Is It and How to Combat It
author: Graham Sheldon (CineD)
why: Why Rec.709 exports look washed out on macOS: NCLC 1-1-1 vs 1-2-1 tags, ColorSync's 1.96 gamma, dim-surround compensation, what platforms retag, and practical viewer and monitoring settings.

title: Adobe color management (Video Post-Production Workflow Guide)
author: Frame.io
why: One consistent Rec.709 setup across Photoshop, Premiere and After Effects: working space, media colour-space overrides, display colour management, and how to fix graphics that come in as sRGB and shift.

title: Color Management in Adobe After Effects
author: ECAbrams
why: Colour spaces, gamut and transfer functions explained, then the actual AE settings (working space, interpret, display, output profile) that keep renders matching the comp.

title: Remove banding in After Effects, Premiere, and everywhere
author: Rich Young (ProVideo Coalition)
why: Banding fixes with exact numbers: 1-5% Noise or Add Grain, 16/32 bpc for precision, AE dithers only when converting down to 8 bpc on render, and an Arithmetic-effect trick to preview the dither.

title: Basics of rendering and exporting
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Full Render Queue reference: render settings (quality, resolution, frame blending, motion blur, time span), output module settings (format, channels, straight/premultiplied alpha, colour, audio), templates, statuses, post-render actions, AME hand-off.

title: Exporting H.264 from the After Effects Render Queue
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Native H.264 from the Render Queue: Format Options (hardware/software encoding, profile/level, bitrate), the 5/15/40 Mbps presets, and how to resolve settings-mismatch warnings.

title: Export settings reference for Media Encoder
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Media Encoder export settings line by line: Match Source, VBR 1/2-pass, target/max bitrate, Key Frame Distance, Render at Maximum Depth, Use Maximum Render Quality, alpha options.

title: RENDER SETTINGS and OUTPUT MODULE in After Effects Tutorial
author: SternFX (Eran Stern)
why: Walks through the Render Queue, the Render Settings and Output Module dialogs section by section, and rendering several outputs from one item; by Eran Stern, with manual captions. Under 50k views and a low like ratio, but a top-tier instructor and current (AE 2023).

title: CD / The Horrors of the Alpha Channel
author: Captain Disillusion
why: The clearest explanation of premultiplication: double-multiplying gives dark edges, treating straight as premultiplied gives ghosting, apps unmultiply, and formats rarely tag which kind they hold; the theory behind our straight-alpha PNG handoff and Interpret Footage choices.

title: Work with Motion Graphics templates
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Essential Graphics panel and MOGRT export: primary comp, supported property controls, groups, font controls, replaceable media, CSV/TSV data controls, comments, export.

title: Essential Properties Explained | Ae Genius
author: Jake In Motion
why: Essential Properties turn one precomp into a reusable element whose chosen properties (texture, randomness, animation controls) can be set per instance without duplicating comps; under 50k views, but recent and 4.7% likes.

title: Memory and storage
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Memory preferences, RAM needed for rendering, purging, RAM/disk/media cache and the persistent disk cache; the settings behind slow previews and long-render memory thrash.
